lines.trans: This tomato-based sauce is really delicious.
Let's order dessert afterwards too, shall we?
It's called dolce, not dessert. That's what they call it in Italy.
Oh my, you really do know all about it.
Mother, listen—someday I want to study abroad in Italy.

examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Marks the subject of existence, emergence, or questions (どれが), and at the end of a polite clause softens a request (のですが).

examples.text: お願いがあるのですが。
examples.trans: I have a favor to ask.

meanings.note: Plain い-adjective.

examples.text: 彼の英語は本当にすごい。

meanings.en: location of action; means; scope total
meanings.note: Marks where an action happens, the unit/scope of a rate or total (十日で, 全部で), or the cause/occasion.

examples.trans: It is one thousand yen in total.

examples.text: あとでデザートも頼みましょうね。
examples.trans: Let's order dessert afterwards too, shall we?

examples.text: デザートじゃなくてドルチェですよ。イタリアではそう呼ぶの。
examples.trans: It's called dolce, not dessert. That's what they call it in Italy.

meanings.note: Replaces は, が, or を to add 'also' or 'too'.

examples.trans: Please give me this one too.

examples.text: あそこも新しい店です。
examples.trans: Over there is a new shop too.

meanings.note: Checks agreement ('isn't it?') or softens a request or farewell.

meanings.en: short casual form of じゃあ / では
meanings.note: Brisk spoken transition before taking the next step.
Negates verbs or forms じゃない ('is not') in questions like いいんじゃないか.

examples.text: デザートじゃなくてドルチェですよ。イタリアではそう呼ぶの。
examples.trans: It's called dolce, not dessert. That's what they call it in Italy.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Polite sentence-ending counterpart of plain だ.

cells: ではありません / じゃありません

meanings.note: Tells the listener something new or adds warm reassurance at the end of a sentence.
More formal counterpart of じゃあ used in business and polite conversation.

meanings.en: in that way; that is so
meanings.note: そうですか ('Is that so? / I see') calmly acknowledges news.

examples.text: そうですか、わかりました。

meanings.note: Links a modifying noun to a following noun, or turns a clause into an explanatory statement (often contracted to ん in speech).
Standard gender-neutral 'I' in polite and business Japanese.

meanings.en: target, location of existence, or result marker
meanings.note: Marks destination, location where something exists or sits, or the chosen result before する and なる.
All-purpose action verb; turns Sino-Japanese nouns into verbs (融通する, 出店する) and with に means 'decide on' or 'make into'.
Marks the presence of a person (責任者はいるか) or follows て-form (often contracted to てる/てます in speech).

examples.text: 本格的に絵のお勉強したくって。
examples.trans: I really want to study painting seriously.

examples.trans: I really want to study painting seriously.

examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Prefixed to native Japanese words (お店, お二人, お持ち帰り) to add politeness.

meanings.en: come; go do something and return (after て-form)
meanings.note: Written in kana after a て-form (話してきます), expresses stepping away to do an action and coming back.

examples.text: ちょっと水を買ってきます。
examples.trans: I will go buy some water and be right back.

meanings.note: With します, forms お願いします ('please'), the standard polite way to request a service or favor.

examples.text: 一つお願いがあります。
examples.trans: I have one favor to ask.

meanings.note: Asks about condition, outcome (どうだった), or what happened (どうしましたか).
Core everyday reassurance or check covering safety, health, and reliability.

examples.text: 心配しないで、大丈夫だよ。
examples.trans: Do not worry, it is fine.

meanings.note: I-adjective; after て-form (～てほしい), means 'want someone to do something'.

examples.trans: I want you to come soon.

examples.text: 諦めてほしくないのです。
examples.trans: I don't want you to give up.

meanings.note: Standard heartfelt apology.

examples.text: ごめんなさい、もうしません。
examples.trans: I'm sorry, I won't do it again.

meanings.note: Written を and pronounced o; marks what an action directly acts upon.
分かってる asks or states ongoing understanding; plain past 分かった means 'got it! / I understand'.

examples.text: 日本語が少し分かります。

examples.trans: Got it, I will come right away.

meanings.note: Standard polite 'goodbye'.
